terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation (-iō); with an accusative, or ut and the subjunctive
evidence: Catull. 76.14: vērum hoc quā lubet efficiās
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to bring to pass, to effect, execute, complete, accomplish”. Often Latin needs no verb for “manage”: the plain verb with tandem, vix or aegrē says it (vix aperuī, I only just managed to open it).

evidence: Traupman 343: sī id cōnficere poteris, if you can manage it

terms.gloss: I get to, I have the chance to (by good fortune)
terms.grammar: verb, impersonal; with the dative, and ut or an infinitive
evidence: Quint. 1.1.7: quibus discere ipsīs nōn contigit
terms.comment: Of what falls to one’s lot, not of effort.

phrases.latin: difficile est longum subitō dēpōnere amōrem, difficile est, vērum hoc quā lubet efficiās
phrases.english: It is hard to lay down a long love all at once; it is hard, but you must manage it somehow.

phrases.latin: nec tamen iī, quibus discere ipsīs nōn contigit, minōrem cūram docendī līberōs habeant
phrases.english: Yet parents who never had the chance to learn should take no less care over teaching their children.
I managed to open it at last!

sources: Lewis & Short: efficio · Lewis & Short: conficio · Lewis & Short: contingo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 343.
